migration.name: 20260724120000_add_backlog_archetype_scope
migration.backfill: additive only. BacklogItem and Epic receive nullable scopeKind/scopeRationale fields and empty-array defaults for archetypeCategories, archetypeIds, and lifecycleTags. The backfill classifies rows only where existing durable signals are present: EP-FABRIC-CARE-OPS and its child items are fabric-care-services/dry-cleaning-plant-network; Industry Vertical Readiness epics map to known category or leaf slugs and child items inherit; finance/payroll/workforce/identity epics become common; platform lifecycle, UX, upgrade, Build Studio, tracking, and data-governance epics become platform. Ambiguous rows stay null/empty for operator review.

changes.lifecycleDisposition: retained with the epic as planning metadata; archive/delete semantics remain unchanged and scope fields do not create new lifecycle ownership

fields.reason: separates platform, common, category-specific, leaf-specific, multi-archetype, and unknown roadmap work without overloading portfolio alignment
records the archetype category slugs served by the epic so portfolio review can see category gaps explicitly
records leaf archetype slugs such as dry-cleaning-plant-network when work is specific to one business operating model
keeps the human classification rationale close to the planning row so ambiguous items can be reviewed without reconstructing intent from titles
captures product/service lifecycle tags such as claim-ticket, ready-promise, booking, or invoice for roadmap and budget slicing

changes.lifecycleDisposition: retained with the backlog item as execution planning metadata; existing status, triage, claim, build, and completion lifecycles remain authoritative

fields.reason: lets individual items inherit, narrow, or override epic-level scope when one epic contains mixed platform/common/archetype work
supports explicit category filtering in MCP tools, REST routes, and workbook review
supports leaf-specific gap tracking for archetypes such as dry-cleaning-plant-network without creating a one-off portfolio
preserves the operator or agent rationale for scope tagging so later roadmap reviews can correct the classification deliberately
groups archetype-specific work by operating lifecycle step, for example claim-ticket custody versus ready-promise notifications
